EUR-JPY -

Does anyone have insights in to why this trade failed?

I entered a long position (as shown in post # 603) and price bounced nicely. I was up over 40 pips, and price was approaching my limit, when price tanked. author: hoeschec
text:
I am looking at post #503 in Salivan's Journal called 'Art of War".

He recently posted a trade on EUR-USD which I still can't understand. If I had been looking at the charts live, I would not have seen this as an opportunity. This tells me I need to investigate and challenge myself to improve my understanding. Here I go:

The trade was executed on a 1 min chart (EUR-USD).

I recreated the chart he posted with all of his original markings to use as a basis for my analysis moving forward. Here is what his chart looked like:

This shows his entry:

author: hoeschec
text:
(Continued from last post)

First, I am zooming out to look at the bigger picture to see if price was entering an obvious Demand/FTR/FL etc... from above. I typically start on higher time frame charts to ID opportunities before dropping down to lower time frames. Here is what I wold have seen on Salivan's trade:

What I see:

1. Price initially enters a zone where I would definitely expect a bounce. Price enters a strong demand zone (fresh) which also served as the origin of the previous move up. There is also a QM level in this demand zone (as I show on the chart).. If you look closely however, Salivan takes the trade on price's second return (deeper) in to this demand zone. I wouldn't have been looking for buys after price initially broke in and broke out of the demand zone. I probably would have switched to a different chart if I had been watching live, thinking the best bounce was the bounce that occurred on price's FTB.

Let's zoom in and see what else is showing....

author: hoeschec
text:
(Continued from last post)

Here is a close up view of the EUR-USD chart (15 M) that shows the original demand zone (located way to the left of where Salivan actually executed his trade). The dotted red line shows the exact price where he bought. I did a close up of this area but can't find any price structure that would suggest price was going to bounce at this level. I don't see a FL/FTR/Origin/Decision point etc...

The only thing I see here, is price made an obvious fakeout to the downside before breaking back to the upside.

Hmmm...

author: hoeschec
text:
(continued)

I have zoomed in to look at the main area depicted in Salivan's trade. His rectangles are included in this chart, but I have added my own rectangle (neon green) to show how I would have drawn the zone.

Why did Salivan draw the rectangle the way he did (rectangle labeled 1)? I would have drawn the FTR with the neon green rectangle (labeled # 2). This difference in how we draw the zones matters later on when he marks price as engulfed....I wouldn't have seen an engulf until price broke through the top of the Neon rectangle. He labeled PA an engulf when it broke the high of rectangle # 1.

Maybe he wasn't labeling the FTR- maybe he labeled the origin of the engulf down, and saw this was important zone because it was the flag that held price down twice before it engulfed and retested to create a swap zone?... Here is a chart showing this theory:

author: hoeschec
text:
Continued-

The next chart I am posting shows the second rectangle (Labeled Rectangle 2) Salivan draws- the only significance I can see of rectangle #2 is it is the origin of the engulf that proceeds it, and this is a flag that holds price down when it returns (labeled zone A). If this is true, why does Salivan ignore the engulf of rectangle # 2 (labeled EG A on the chart below)? He only labels the engulf of the first rectangle (labeled as EG B on chart below). Was the the engulf of Rectangle 1 more significant because it formed first?
